title: First-Level Fourier Cost Bound
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $0<p<1$, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, and let $T$ be a zero-error randomized decision tree computing $f$. For the product distribution in which each coordinate is $-1$ with probability $p$ and $1$ with probability $1-p$, the sum of the biased Fourier coefficients of $f$ on the singleton sets is at most the product of the square roots of the second moment of $f$ and the average query cost of $T$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on the sign cube
$T$ is a randomized decision tree computing $f`
